title: Syntax-Diversified Unlearning: Evaluating Data-Side Interventions for Reducing Worst-Case Leakage

contributions.purpose: Test the hypothesis that syntactic diversification of forget queries reduces worst-case sampling leakage and benign relearning vulnerability in LLM unlearning.
contributions.mechanism: Implement a paraphrase-based augmentation pipeline that adds syntactically diverse variants of forget queries to the forget set during NPO unlearning on TOFU forget10.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated via leak@32 worst-case sampling leakage and relearning vulnerability on TOFU forget10 (400 forget QA pairs, 3,600 retain pairs) with Negative Preference Optimization.
contributions.source_quote: We test the hypothesis that syntactic diversification of forget queries reduces worst-case sampling leakage (leak@32) and benign relearning vulnerability, motivated by recent findings on syntax-driven unlearning failures.

contributions.purpose: Provide a rigorous pre-registered evaluation protocol for the data-side unlearning intervention.
contributions.mechanism: Define pre-specified success criteria (>=20% leak@32 reduction, >=0.10 Relearn SR reduction, <=3% utility drop) and run experiments across multiple random seeds.
contributions.evaluation: Success criteria checked against measured outcomes: leak@32 dropped from 0.167 to 0.133 at low temperature (20% relative reduction) but relearning threshold was not met.
contributions.source_quote: We conduct rigorous evaluation with pre-specified success criteria (>=20% leak@32 reduction, >=0.10 Relearn SR reduction, <=3% utility drop) and multiple random seeds.

contributions.purpose: Report a negative result showing data-side interventions alone cannot fix fundamental unlearning vulnerabilities.
contributions.mechanism: Compare the syntax-diversified intervention against baseline NPO on relearning vulnerability and worst-case leakage metrics.
contributions.evaluation: The intervention fails to meaningfully reduce relearning vulnerability (0.017 vs the 0.10 threshold) despite marginal leak@32 improvement at low temperature.
contributions.source_quote: We report a negative result: the intervention fails to meaningfully reduce relearning vulnerability (0.017 vs 0.10 threshold) despite marginal improvement in leak@32 at low temperature, suggesting that data-side interventions alone are insufficient to address fundamental unlearning vulnerabilities.

self_declared_provenance.quote: These methods predominantly focus on optimization-level interventions; data-side approaches that modify the forget set itself remain underexplored.

Yoon et al. (2026) specifically identify syntax as a hidden driver of unlearning failures, finding that models may learn to suppress specific syntactic patterns rather than the underlying knowledge. These findings suggest that syntactic diversification during unlearning might help address these vulnerabilities, motivating our investigation.
We evaluate our approach on the TOFU benchmark (Maini et al., 2024), a controlled testbed for LLM unlearning... We use the forget10 setting.

notes: Explicit NEGATIVE-RESULT paper (declared in abstract and contribution list): hypothesis-driven data-side intervention showed only marginal leak@32 improvement and failed the pre-specified relearning criterion. Paper positions the failure as evidence for representation-level solutions.
